audit.whatIsWrong: Blood Hunt (W) is described as an unconditional sticking tool — "his W move speed sticks on you", "Use W move speed to stick on you" — with no mention of its health gate.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Warwick senses enemies below 50% health, gaining Move Speed toward and attack speed against them. When they fall below 25% health, he frenzies and these bonuses triple." At full HP, Blood Hunt gives him nothing. The entire early lane advice is built on a threat that only exists once Nasus is already under half, and it hides the single cleanest piece of counterplay in the matchup: stay above 50% and his chase does not turn on.
audit.corrected: Blood Hunt only grants speed toward you below 50% HP and triples below 25%. Staying above half switches it off entirely.

audit.whatIsWrong: "his Q heals every auto" and "Q heal-on-attack" attribute an on-auto-attack heal to Jaws of the Beast.
audit.why: Jaws of the Beast is a single lunge-bite on 8/7.5/7/6.5/6 that heals for damage dealt — not an auto-attack effect. The heal-on-basic-attack is Eternal Hunger (P), and only below 50% health. Merging the two produces a Warwick who appears to heal continuously from level 1, which he does not, and it hides that his auto sustain is switched on by Nasus chipping him low.
audit.corrected: Jaws of the Beast is an 8s lunge that heals for damage dealt. The on-auto heal is Eternal Hunger (P), active only below 50% HP.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Save Wither for the instant he W-dashes in" — Blood Hunt is not a dash.
audit.why: kitFlags.dash lists Q and R. Blood Hunt is a scan-and-mark with no movement of its own. A Nasus holding Wither for a W-dash that cannot happen mistimes the only defensive cooldown he has before 6.
audit.corrected: His gap-closers are Jaws of the Beast (Q, 365-range lunge) and Infinite Duress (R). Wither the Q lunge.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer states that Infinite Duress's leap distance scales with Warwick's bonus move speed.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Warwick leaps in a direction (scaling with his bonus Move Speed), suppressing the first champion he collides with." This makes Wither a range-check on his ultimate, not just a post-hoc slow — and it chains with the Blood Hunt gate, because the bonus move speed Blood Hunt grants toward a sub-50% target is exactly what extends the leap. Staying above half HP shortens his ult. This is the most decisive unstated interaction in the matchup and it is the kind of thing that decides whether a river walk is safe.
audit.corrected: Infinite Duress leaps further the more bonus move speed he has. Wither shortens it, and staying above 50% HP denies him the Blood Hunt speed that lengthens it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl (E) is never mentioned once, in either layer.
audit.why: It is damage reduction for 2.5 seconds that ends in a 1-second flee on nearby enemies, on 15/14/13/12/11. For Nasus specifically this is the ability that ruins the matchup's whole plan: the stacked Siphoning Strike he has been saving lands into a damage-reduction window, and the fear then breaks the auto-attack chain and the Wither chase. Omitting it means the guide never tells the reader when not to spend their one big hit.
audit.corrected: Never dump a stacked Q into Primal Howl — 2.5s of damage reduction on 15s at rank 1, ending in a 1s fear that breaks your chase. Bait it, then commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names only Infinite Duress and gives no number for it or anything else.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is 110/90/70 — the longest real window in his kit and the one worth playing around. Primal Howl at 15/14/13/12/11 is the short cooldown that actually decides individual trades, and at rank 1 it matches Wither's own 15s exactly, so the two come back together and the trade pattern repeats on a clean loop.
audit.corrected: Infinite Duress 110s at rank 1. Primal Howl 15s at rank 1 — the same as Wither, so they return together.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game plan leans on Fury of the Sands' bonus health without noting that Jaws of the Beast is max-health damage.
audit.why: Q "deal[s] damage based on their maximum health" and carries the percentHealth flag. Nasus's own ultimate grants bonus Health, so popping R against Warwick inflates the size of his single biggest hit. Raw HP and raw armour are both partly wrong answers here; the working answer is Grievous Wounds against the three separate heals on P, Q and R.
audit.corrected: Fury of the Sands' bonus health feeds Jaws of the Beast's max-health damage. Anti-heal is the item that actually moves this matchup — he heals off P, Q and R.
sources: champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json — needs-antiheal and resistances-invalidated, nasus vs warwick

audit.whatIsWrong: "slowing his attack speed dries up his Q heal" — Wither's attack-speed component does not affect Jaws of the Beast's heal.
audit.why: Q heals for damage dealt by one bite; it is not attack-speed gated. What the attack-speed slow actually starves is Eternal Hunger, the on-auto heal. The advice is right for the wrong reason, which matters because it implies Wither shuts off his burst sustain when it does not.
audit.corrected: Wither's attack-speed cut starves Eternal Hunger's on-auto heal; the move-speed cut is what touches his engage.

edits.after: Blood Hunt gives him nothing until you drop under 50% HP, but Jaws of the Beast bites for max health — stay healthy, concede.

edits.after: Eternal Hunger heals him only under 50% HP and triples under 25% — chipping him low switches his sustain on.

edits.after: Wither lands at 3 — the attack-speed cut starves Eternal Hunger's on-auto heal, the move-speed cut shortens his Infinite Duress leap.

edits.before: Warwick owns these levels — his W move speed sticks to you and his Q heals every auto, so he wins any extended trade before your Wither is up. Don't try to duel him at 1 or 2; just last-hit with Q and chunk him with Spirit Fire (E) to shred his armor and deny clean drain trades. At 3 your Wither flips the chase math — slow his attack speed and move speed and his passive heal starves out — but he still edges the all-in if you let him stack autos.
edits.after: Warwick owns these levels, but not the way it looks: Blood Hunt gives him nothing until you fall under 50% HP, and the heal on his autos is Eternal Hunger (P), which is gated the same way. Jaws of the Beast (Q) is the real early threat — an 8s lunge that bites for your max health. Last-hit with Q, chunk him with Spirit Fire (E) to shred armor, and stay above half so neither gate opens. At 3 Wither flips the chase math, but he still edges a full all-in.

edits.before: Now you stabilize. Save Wither for the instant he W-dashes in: cutting his attack speed kills both his Q heal and low-HP passive sustain, turning his drain fight into a one-sided grind. At 6 Fury of the Sands is your real swing — the bonus health, percent-HP magic burn and Q damage boost let you survive or win his committed all-in, and your lifesteal eats his DPS while Wither holds him in place. Bait the R-into-drain; once it's down he has no second engage.
edits.after: Now you stabilize. Save Wither for the instant Jaws of the Beast lunges in: the attack-speed cut starves Eternal Hunger, and the move-speed cut shortens Infinite Duress, which leaps further the more bonus move speed he carries. Never dump a stacked Q into Primal Howl (E) — 2.5s of damage reduction on 15s at rank 1, ending in a 1s fear that breaks your chase. Bait it, then commit. At 6 Fury of the Sands lets you survive or win his all-in.

edits.before: This evens out into a pure attrition duel and you have the tools for it — stacked Q plus Wither plus your ult out-sustains his drain, and percent-HP magic from Fury answers his bruiser HP. The one thing that beats you is his R suppress setting up a gank: the channel locks you in place with no escape, so never walk up near river with Wither on cooldown. Win the straight 1v1, but respect that his lockdown turns a 1v1 you'd win into a 2v1 you lose.
edits.after: This evens out into a pure attrition duel and you have the tools for it — stacked Q plus Wither out-grinds his drain, provided you carry Grievous Wounds, because he heals off P, Q and R. Watch one trap: Fury of the Sands' bonus health feeds Jaws of the Beast, which damages off your max HP. Infinite Duress is what actually beats you — a 1.5s suppression that leaps further the more bonus move speed he has, so never face him near river with Wither down.

notes: This was the weakest entry in my slice and got the most work. Three separate abilities were described wrongly and a fourth (Primal Howl) was absent from both layers entirely. The most useful thing recovered from the kit file is the chain Blood Hunt -> bonus move speed -> Infinite Duress leap distance: staying above 50% HP literally shortens the range of his ultimate, which no version of this text said. I did not touch anything about whether the suppression can be cleansed or QSS'd — nasus/warwick needsResearch is empty, which means unknown, so I left the topic alone rather than assert. Same full-vs-content level-chart contradiction noted in nasus__volibear applies here (full gives Warwick stages 1-4, content gives Skill at 3 and 4); not submittable as an edit under the length band.
